title: Meet A, B and C
goal: Recognise A, B and C, match a, b and c, and say their letter names.
cue: A letter has a name. Later, we will learn the sounds it can represent in words. Today, say the letter names.
spelling: A letter has a name. Later, we will learn the sounds it can represent in words. Today, say the letter names.
task: Point to A and C. Say their names, then write their lowercase partners.
story: The letter A has a big form and a small form.
reviewPrompt: Say the letters you already know. Then name one new letter.

articulation.label: Letter A
articulation.alt: Letter A: /eɪ/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /ɪ/: Raise the front tongue; narrow the jaw gap.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.

cards.title: Letter B
sections: ball /bɔl/ · a round object for games
The letter name is /bi/. In ball, b starts with /b/: close both lips briefly, then release into the vowel. Do not add “uh” or use “bee” when blending. Hear the word in “This is a ball.”
Write B and b three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

articulation.label: Letter B
articulation.alt: Letter B: /b/ → /i/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /b/: Close lips briefly; release into the next vowel.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Letter C
sections: cat /kæt/ · an animal that says meow

Write C and c three times. Cover the model and write the pair again.

cards.title: Five words to hear and use
sections: a round fruit with red or green skin. She puts the apple back in the bowl.
a round object for games. The ball is under the chair.
an animal that says meow. The cat sleeps on the bed.
A small insect that lives in a group. An ant is on the leaf.
a container used to carry things. The key is inside his bag, under a book.
Listen to each word. Point or act to show its meaning. Say one word, then one short sentence. Ask for help with spelling patterns you have not learned yet.
